description: Achievements focused on team workflows, shared knowledge, and collaborative development practices with Claude Code

architecture_doc.longDescription: Document your project's architecture decisions directly in CLAUDE.md so Claude understands the reasoning behind your system design. Include ADRs (Architecture Decision Records), component diagrams references, and design rationale. This creates persistent context that helps Claude suggest changes aligned with your architectural vision, and helps new team members understand why the system is built the way it is.
architecture_doc.whyItMatters: Architecture context prevents Claude from suggesting changes that violate design principles. It creates institutional memory that persists across sessions and team members.

howTo.summary: Add an Architecture or Design Decisions section to your project CLAUDE.md documenting key architectural choices.
steps: Create or open your project's CLAUDE.md file in the repository root
Add an ## Architecture section with an overview of the system design
Document key design decisions with rationale: 'We use X because Y'
Reference any ADR documents: 'See docs/adr/ for detailed decision records'

examples.title: Architecture section in CLAUDE.md
examples.code:
## Architecture

This project follows a hexagonal architecture pattern:
- `src/domain/` - Core business logic, no external dependencies
- `src/adapters/` - External service integrations
- `src/ports/` - Interface definitions

### Design Decisions
- ADR-001: We use PostgreSQL over MongoDB for ACID compliance
- ADR-002: Event sourcing for audit trail requirements
- ADR-003: Feature flags via LaunchDarkly for gradual rollouts

When making changes, preserve the separation between domain and adapters.

tips: Keep architecture docs high-level but actionable for Claude
Update when major architectural changes are made
Link to detailed ADR documents rather than duplicating content
Include diagrams as ASCII art or references to image files

code_review_giver.longDescription: Leverage Claude to provide thoughtful code reviews on pull requests or code shared by teammates. Claude can analyze code for bugs, security issues, performance problems, and adherence to coding standards. You can share PR URLs, paste code snippets, or ask Claude to review changes in your local repository. This accelerates the review process while maintaining code quality standards.
code_review_giver.whyItMatters: Automated code review catches issues early, reduces reviewer fatigue, and ensures consistent application of coding standards across the team.

howTo.summary: Ask Claude to review code from pull requests, commits, or shared snippets for quality and issues.
steps: Share a PR URL or paste code you want reviewed
Ask Claude to review for specific concerns: security, performance, style
Request Claude explain any issues found with suggested fixes
Use the feedback to improve the code before merging

tips: Be specific about what aspects you want reviewed
Include relevant context like coding standards or security requirements
Use /review-pr command if available for structured reviews

commit_crafter.longDescription: Create a custom slash command that generates standardized commit messages for your team. The command can enforce conventional commits format, include ticket references, run pre-commit checks, and ensure consistent messaging across all contributors. This automates the tedious parts of committing while maintaining a clean, searchable git history.
commit_crafter.whyItMatters: Consistent commit messages improve git history readability, enable automated changelog generation, and make code archeology much easier for the team.

howTo.summary: Create a commit.md command file that generates commits following your team's conventions.
steps: Create the directory: mkdir -p .claude/commands
Create .claude/commands/commit.md with your commit template
Define the commit message format (conventional commits, etc.)
Include instructions for extracting ticket numbers from branch names
Test with /commit in a Claude Code session

examples.title: Conventional commits command
examples.code:
---
description: Create a conventional commit with ticket reference
---

Analyze the staged changes and create a commit message following this format:

```
<type>(<scope>): <description>

[optional body]

Refs: <ticket-from-branch>
```

Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore

Extract ticket number from branch name (e.g., feature/PROJ-123-foo -> PROJ-123).

Keep the description under 72 characters.
Explain WHY in the body, not WHAT (the diff shows what).

tips: Include your team's specific commit conventions
Add ticket number extraction from branch names
Consider adding pre-commit hook integration
Keep the command focused - use separate commands for complex workflows

convention_keeper.longDescription: Define your team's coding standards, naming conventions, and style guidelines directly in CLAUDE.md. When Claude understands your conventions, it generates code that matches your existing codebase style automatically. This eliminates style-related code review comments and ensures consistency whether Claude or humans write the code.
convention_keeper.whyItMatters: Documented conventions reduce code review friction, accelerate onboarding, and ensure Claude-generated code integrates seamlessly with existing code.

howTo.summary: Add a Conventions or Style Guide section to CLAUDE.md documenting your team's coding standards.
steps: Create or open CLAUDE.md in your project root
Add a ## Conventions or ## Style Guide section
Document naming patterns: files, functions, variables, classes
Include code organization rules and import ordering
Add examples of preferred patterns

examples.title: Conventions section in CLAUDE.md
examples.code:
## Conventions

### Naming
- Components: PascalCase (UserProfile.tsx)
- Hooks: camelCase with 'use' prefix (useAuth.ts)
- Utils: camelCase (formatDate.ts)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
- CSS classes: kebab-case

### Code Style
- Prefer named exports over default exports
- Use async/await over .then() chains
- Destructure props in function parameters
- Maximum function length: 50 lines

### File Organization
- One component per file
- Colocate tests: Component.test.tsx
- Group by feature, not by type

tips: Be specific with examples, not just rules
Include anti-patterns to avoid
Reference your ESLint/Prettier config if applicable
Update conventions as team practices evolve

doc_collaborator.longDescription: Create a documentation command that helps your team generate and maintain project documentation consistently. The command can create README sections, API documentation, component docs, or user guides following your team's documentation standards. This ensures documentation stays current and follows a consistent format.
doc_collaborator.whyItMatters: Automated documentation workflows reduce the friction of keeping docs updated. Consistent templates make documentation more useful and easier to maintain.

howTo.summary: Create a docs.md or document.md command that generates documentation following team standards.

Define your documentation template and format

# Component Name

Read the component source code and generate accurate documentation.

Add context about your documentation tools (Storybook, Docusaurus, etc.)
Consider separate commands for different doc types

The command can create GitHub or Linear issues with proper labels, link issues to code, or help triage and prioritize the backlog. This integrates your issue tracking directly into the development flow, reducing context switching.
issue_tracker.whyItMatters: Integrated issue tracking reduces context switching and ensures issues are created with proper detail, labels, and context from the start.

howTo.summary: Create an issue.md or bug.md command that interfaces with your issue tracking system.
steps: Create .claude/commands/issue.md or bug.md
Define the issue template your team uses
Include instructions for adding labels, assignees, and links
Add context extraction from current code or errors
Test with /issue or /bug in a session

examples.title: GitHub issue creation command
examples.code:
---
description: Create a GitHub issue with proper formatting
---

Create a GitHub issue following our team template.

Gather this information:
1. Issue title (clear, actionable)
2. Type: bug, feature, enhancement, or chore
3. Priority: P0 (critical), P1 (high), P2 (medium), P3 (low)
4. Detailed description with steps to reproduce (for bugs)

Use this format:
```
gh issue create --title "<title>" \
  --label "<type>,priority:<priority>" \
  --body "## Description
<description>

## Steps to Reproduce
<steps>

## Expected Behavior
<expected>

## Actual Behavior
<actual>"
```

If context from current code is relevant, include file references.

tips: Include your team's label taxonomy
Add template sections for different issue types
Consider integration with Linear, Jira, or other tools via CLI
Include automatic context from current file or error messages

knowledge_sharer.longDescription: Build a comprehensive project CLAUDE.md with 10 or more well-organized sections documenting team patterns, conventions, architecture, and workflows. This creates a rich knowledge base that helps Claude provide highly contextual assistance and serves as living documentation for the entire team. The more context you provide, the better Claude understands your project.
knowledge_sharer.whyItMatters: Comprehensive documentation enables Claude to provide expert-level assistance specific to your project. It preserves institutional knowledge that benefits current and future team members.

Review and update regularly as the project evolves

mentorship.longDescription: Use Claude as a learning companion by asking it to explain code concepts, design patterns, or technology choices in your codebase. Claude can break down complex code, explain the reasoning behind architectural decisions, or teach new programming concepts in context. This transforms code exploration into an educational experience.
mentorship.whyItMatters: Contextual learning accelerates skill development. Understanding the 'why' behind code helps you make better decisions and contribute more effectively.

howTo.summary: Ask Claude to explain code concepts, patterns, or decisions in educational detail.

Ask 'explain how this works' or 'why is it built this way'

Ask for real-world analogies when concepts are abstract
Request pros and cons of different approaches
Use 'explain like I'm a junior developer' for fundamentals

Include setup instructions, key concepts, important files to review, and common workflows. This transforms the onboarding experience by giving new developers an AI-powered guide who knows the codebase.
onboarding_guide.whyItMatters: Structured onboarding reduces ramp-up time for new team members and ensures they learn the right patterns from day one.

steps: Add an ## Onboarding or ## Getting Started section to CLAUDE.md

examples.title: Onboarding section in CLAUDE.md
examples.code:
## Onboarding

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 20+
- Docker Desktop
- Access to 1Password vault 'Engineering'

### Setup Steps
1. Clone repo and run `npm install`
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local`
3. Get secrets: `op read op://Engineering/app-secrets`
4. Start services: `docker-compose up -d`
5. Run migrations: `npm run db:migrate`
6. Start dev server: `npm run dev`

### Key Areas to Understand First
- `src/domain/` - Core business logic
- `src/api/` - API routes and handlers
- `docs/architecture.md` - System design

### First Week Checklist
- [ ] Complete local setup
- [ ] Review architecture docs
- [ ] Shadow a PR review
- [ ] Make a small bug fix

tips: Include common 'gotchas' new developers encounter
Link to video walkthroughs or detailed docs
Add team contacts for different areas
Keep setup steps tested and current

pr_automator.longDescription: Create a command that automates your team's pull request workflow. The command can generate PR descriptions, create PRs with proper labels and reviewers, or prepare branches for review. This ensures every PR follows team standards and includes necessary context for reviewers.
pr_automator.whyItMatters: Consistent PR workflows improve review quality and speed. Automated PR creation ensures nothing is forgotten and reviewers have the context they need.

howTo.summary: Create a pr.md or review-pr.md command that streamlines your pull request process.
steps: Create .claude/commands/pr.md or pull-request.md
Define your PR template and required sections
Include instructions for generating descriptions from commits
Add reviewer assignment and labeling logic
Test with /pr in a session

examples.title: PR creation command
examples.code:
---
description: Create a pull request with proper formatting
---

Create a pull request for the current branch following our team standards.

1. Analyze all commits since branching from main
2. Generate a PR description with:
   - Summary of changes (2-3 sentences)
   - List of key changes (bullet points)
   - Testing notes
   - Screenshots if UI changes (prompt user)

3. Extract ticket number from branch name for title prefix

4. Create PR:
```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "[TICKET-123] Clear description" \
  --body "<generated body>" \
  --label "needs-review" \
  --reviewer "@org/team-reviewers"
```

Include a ## Test Plan section with verification steps.

tips: Include your team's PR template structure
Add automatic reviewer assignment based on files changed
Consider a separate review-pr.md for reviewing incoming PRs
Include checklist items for common PR requirements

release_manager.longDescription: Create a command that streamlines your release process - generating changelogs, creating release notes, or preparing version bumps. The command can analyze commits since the last release, categorize changes by type, and produce release documentation that keeps stakeholders informed about what changed and why.
release_manager.whyItMatters: Automated release workflows reduce human error and ensure consistent, informative release notes. Stakeholders stay informed without manual documentation effort.

howTo.summary: Create a release.md or changelog.md command that automates release documentation.
steps: Create .claude/commands/release.md or changelog.md
Define your changelog format (Keep a Changelog, etc.)
Include commit parsing for categorization
Add version bumping logic (semver)
Test with /release in a session

examples.title: Release notes command
examples.code:
---
description: Generate release notes and update changelog
---

Generate release notes for the upcoming release.

1. Get commits since last tag: `git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --oneline`

2. Categorize changes:
   - Added: New features (feat:)
   - Changed: Modifications (refactor:, perf:)
   - Fixed: Bug fixes (fix:)
   - Security: Security patches
   - Deprecated: Deprecation notices
   - Removed: Removed features

3. Suggest version bump based on changes:
   - MAJOR: Breaking changes
   - MINOR: New features
   - PATCH: Bug fixes only

4. Update CHANGELOG.md with new section

5. Output release notes for GitHub release body

Follow Keep a Changelog format: https://keepachangelog.com

tips: Use conventional commits for easier categorization
Include breaking change detection for major versions
Consider separate commands for changelog vs full release
Add integration with your release tooling (semantic-release, etc.)

retro_generator.longDescription: Create a command that helps generate retrospective content from your development activity. retro_generator.whyItMatters: Data-driven retrospectives surface patterns that memory alone might miss. Automated summaries ensure comprehensive coverage of the iteration's work.

Add prompts for what went well and improvement areas
Test with /retro in a session

Link to specific PRs or issues for discussion

shared_commands.longDescription: Create three or more custom commands in your project's .claude/commands directory that the entire team can use. shared_commands.whyItMatters: Shared commands create consistency across the team and codify best practices. Once created, they benefit everyone without duplicating effort.

Share with team so they can use /command-name

Keep commands focused on one task each
Document commands in your project README
Iterate on commands based on team feedback

standup_automator.longDescription: Create a command that generates daily standup summaries from your git activity. standup_automator.whyItMatters: Automated standup prep ensures comprehensive updates and saves the mental effort of reconstructing what you worked on.

howTo.summary: Create a standup.md or daily.md command that generates standup updates from recent activity.
steps: Create .claude/commands/standup.md or daily.md
Define your standup format (Yesterday/Today/Blockers)
Include git log analysis for recent commits
Add PR and issue context if available
Test with /standup in a session

examples.title: Standup generation command
examples.code:
---
description: Generate daily standup update
---

Generate my standup update based on recent activity.

1. Yesterday (last working day):
   - Analyze commits from yesterday
   - Check PRs merged or updated
   - List completed work

2. Today:
   - Look at open PRs needing attention
   - Check assigned issues
   - Suggest likely focus areas

3. Blockers:
   - Note any failing CI
   - Pending reviews needed
   - Questions or dependencies

Format for Slack:
```
*Yesterday:*
- Completed X
- Reviewed Y

*Today:*
- Will work on Z
- Planning to finish A

*Blockers:*
- None / Waiting on B
```

tips: Customize the time window (since yesterday vs last 24 hours)
Include PR review activity if relevant
Add team-specific standup format
Consider Slack or Teams formatting
